extracted.intended_audience: Citizens considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution; readers of The Federalist Papers / general public interested in constitutional powers
extracted.subtask_description: An 18th‑century Federalist essay (Madison/Publius) explaining and defending the specific powers conferred by the proposed U.S. Constitution, enumerating classes of federal authority and justifying each. It addresses practical defects of the Articles of Confederation and the reasons for the new provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of foreign consuls
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority concerning the admission of foreign consuls into the United States, particularly where treaties of commerce stipulate mutual appointment of consuls or where existing powers are ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that admission of consuls is sometimes tied to commercial treaties; absent such treaties admission was not clearly provided for under the Confederation. Notes the Convention supplied this omission to avoid ad hoc assumptions of power by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to define and punish piracies and felonies on the high seas and offenses against the law of nations
rubrics_metrics.description: General government authority to define and punish piracies and felonies committed on the high seas and offenses against the law of nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues this power properly belongs to the general government because the Articles lacked provision for offenses against the law of nations, risking embroilment of the Confederation with foreign powers. Emphasizes need for legislative definitions (felony varies by state) to ensure certainty and uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of foreign commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal authority to regulate commerce with foreign nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed previously as well; rationale is to provide a coherent national commerce policy and avoid states adopting conflicting measures that harm national interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to prohibit importation of slaves (delayed until 1808)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional power to prohibit the importation of slaves, but its immediate exercise was postponed until the year 1808.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges it would have been preferable to prohibit immediately but frames the twenty‑year postponement as a significant humanitarian gain and a step toward eventual abolition; rebuts misconceptions that the clause endorses criminal toleration or prevents beneficial emigration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate commerce among the several States
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal power to regulate interstate commerce to secure harmony and proper intercourse among the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies necessity by pointing to past abuses under the Confederation (states imposing tolls/duties on goods passing through), and by analogies (Switzerland, Germany, Netherlands) showing such restraints prevent animosities and interruptions to public tranquility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of commerce with Indian tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to regulate commerce with Indian tribes without the limitations present in the Articles of Confederation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes Articles' problematic restriction to Indians not members of States and its contradiction with states' legislative rights; argues federal regulation avoids confusion over tribal membership and jurisdictional impossibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to coin money and regulate its value (including foreign coin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to coin money and regulate the value of domestic and foreign coin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains Articles limited Congress to regulating coin struck by itself or states; federal power over foreign coin prevents varying state regulations from destroying uniform value of current coin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment of counterfeiting public securities and coin
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to provide punishment for counterfeiting current coin and public securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a natural adjunct of the authority to secure the value of coin and securities; necessary to protect monetary and financial stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixing standards of weights and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to set uniform standards of weights and measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transferred from the Articles and justified by similar considerations as coin regulation — uniformity facilitates commerce and prevents confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a uniform rule of naturalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal authority to establish a single rule governing naturalization across the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that divergent state naturalization rules have caused confusion and could create absurdities (aliens naturalized in one state acquiring rights over another). Uniformity prevents legal evasions and serious embarrassments experienced under the Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish uniform laws of bankruptcy
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to enact uniform bankruptcy laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tied to regulation of commerce — uniform bankruptcy laws will prevent many frauds when parties or property cross state lines, and their expediency is not seriously questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribe proof and effect of public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of each State in other States
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to enact general laws determining how public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of one State are proved and what effect they have in other States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called an evident improvement over the Articles' indeterminate clause; will be convenient for justice, especially on borders where proceedings and effects may transfer across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish post offices and post roads
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to establish post offices and post roads to facilitate intercourse between States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as harmless and potentially greatly convenient; anything facilitating interstate intercourse merits public care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote the progress of science and useful arts (copyrights and patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to secure for limited times to authors and inventors the exclusive right to their writings and discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified as aligning public good with private claims; states cannot separately make effective provisions, and many states had already enacted laws at Congress's instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive legislation over the federal district and federal properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to exercise exclusive legislation over the federal district (not exceeding ten miles square) and over places purchased for forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards, and other needful buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains necessity for complete authority at the seat of government to avoid dependence on a single State and to secure public property; concurrence of ceded State and protections for inhabitants anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to declare punishment of treason with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to define and declare punishment for treason, but prohibiting attainder of treason from working corruption of blood or forfeiture beyond the life of the convict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: United States must be able to punish treason, but constitutional safeguards guard against expansive or politically motivated treason definitions and penalties that extend beyond the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit new States into the Union with restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to admit new States, with prohibitions on forming a new State within the jurisdiction of any other State or forming a State by junction of two or more States or parts without consent of legislatures concerned and Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses omission in the Articles; the precautions guard against hostile partitioning or forced junctions and balance the jealousies of larger and smaller States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispose of and make rules regarding federal territory and property
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to dispose of and make regulations respecting territory or other property belonging to the United States, with proviso not to prejudice claims of the U.S. or any particular State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for managing Western territory and other federal property; proviso aims to allay jealousies and protect existing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee republican form of government and protect States
rubrics_metrics.description: Guarantee to every State of a republican form of government and authority to protect each against invasion and, on application, against domestic violence (when legislature cannot be convened, the executive may apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified as preserving the union's republican character and as a remedy when State governments are endangered; explains scope (guarantee presumes a preexisting republican form) and that federal interposition is intended to prevent or remedy serious threats where State authority fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume and honor pre-existing public debts and engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that all debts contracted and engagements entered into before adoption of the Constitution remain valid against the United States under the new Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as declaratory and designed to reassure foreign creditors; authors argue reciprocity implies validity on both sides and the clause addresses realistic concerns rather than imaginary dangers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide for amendments (three fourths ratification with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power and mode for amending the Constitution — amendments to be ratified by three fourths of the States, with two specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed to guard against excessive mutability and against permanent defect; exceptions (including protection of Senate equality) protect residuary sovereignty and state interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification by nine States sufficient to establish Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that ratification by conventions in nine States is sufficient to establish the Constitution between the ratifying States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified by necessity and self-preservation; unanimous ratification would enable a single State to block essential interests. Discusses delicate questions about superseding the Confederation and relations with non‑ratifying States, arguing moral relations persist though political compacts differ.
